messages.text:
Good morning and to whom it may concern.  Gentlemen after receiving my miners and having some time to try and set them up. One of the Lilygo screens was damaged. As you can see by the picture in the state these miners were sent,(everything was together, PSUs banging around the sealed miners- not packed very well) it’s no wonder the screen was damaged. Can HD please send me a replacement Lilygo? I also tried to flash the Harlo OS but kept getting error messages. I remember seeing something about that the Hammer
DC02  are manufactured with burned eFuses and Secure Boot permanently enabled in the factory. Does this mean that because of the Lilygo I can only stay with hammer miner io?
Searched the web · Hammer DC02 secure boot eFuse Harlo OS flash
Handed to the team · Replacement part (LilyGo T-Display) needs a person to send, and the Harlo OS fla

Good morning Ramces,

Thanks for the photos, I opened both. The first one shows a DC02 powered up with the LilyGo lit and the stats screen running, green power LED, fan fitted. The second one shows the box as it reached you, with the power supplies and cables loose on top of the bagged units. That packing is not how those should travel and I am sorry it arrived that way.

On the damaged LilyGo: a cracked or dead screen on a DC02 is a part, not a board fault, so the miner itself stays with you. I have written up my findings on your order and named the part, and a colleague is picking that up today. If you can send one more photo showing the damaged screen on its own, it makes their job quicker, since the unit in the photo you sent looks to be displaying fine.

On the eFuse and Secure Boot question, the short answer is no, you are not stuck on hammer miner io. I checked the Harlo OS model list this morning and the Hammer DC02 is a supported model, with owners in the Harlo Labs Discord flashing DC02s and reporting they fired right up. I found nothing from Harlo Labs saying our DC02s come with eFuses burned and Secure Boot locked. So a failed flash is far more likely to be the cable, the port or the browser than a locked chip.

Two things worth knowing before you try again. The L. on a DC02 is the controller itself, so you flash through the LilyGo's own USB-C port, with the screen lifted off or the USB connected directly, and you must use a real USB data cable, not a charge-only one. Use Chrome or Edge at harlolabs.com, pick the DC02 profile, then Erase and install the factory image rather than the OTA image for a first flash. Also do not try to flash the unit whose screen is damaged, since a damaged LilyGo will throw errors that look like a firmware problem.

If it still fails, reply with the exact error text the flasher shows, word for word, plus which browser you used and the firmware version it reports. I have already passed this to JD, our hardware lead, with your details. The fastest route to him is our Discord at https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf , mention @nullhashrate, he and the community are on there most of the day and they flash these units constantly.

Hal, HeliumDeploy technical support

Still waiting.
Sent from my iphone

Good morning Ramces,

Apologies for the wait, and here is the full answer so you have something to work with today.

The damaged LilyGo is with the team. My read on it, which they have in writing, is that a screen broken in transit on a DC02 is a part, not a board fault, so the miner itself stays with you and only the LilyGo module needs replacing. I named that part for them and a colleague is picking it up today, so the confirmation on that will come from them. If you can attach one photo of the damaged screen on its own, it will save them a question, since the unit in your first photo appears to be lit and running.

On the eFuse and Secure Boot worry, the short answer is no, you are not locked to hammer miner io. The Hammer DC02 is on the Harlo OS supported model list, and DC02 owners flash it regularly and report it going up first try. I found nothing from Harlo Labs saying our DC02s ship with eFuses burned and Secure Boot permanently on. A flash that errors out is almost always the cable, the port or the browser.

Three things that fix nearly every failed DC02 flash. First, the LilyGo is the controller on this miner, so you flash through the LilyGo's own USB-C port, either with the screen lifted off or with the USB connected directly to it. Second, use a genuine USB data cable, since a charge-only cable will connect power but never show the device to the browser. Third, open harlolabs.com in Chrome or Edge, pick the DC02 profile, and choose Erase and install with the factory image, not the OTA image, for a first flash. One more thing, do not attempt the flash on the unit with the damaged screen, because a damaged LilyGo throws errors that look exactly like a firmware problem.

If it still refuses after that, reply with the exact error text the flasher shows, word for word, along with the browser you used and the version the page reports. JD, our hardware lead, already has your case. The quickest line to him is our Discord at https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf , mention @nullhashrate. He and a lot of DC02 owners are on there through the day.

Hal, HeliumDeploy technical support

This is the BIGGEST ISSUE WITH HELIUMDEPLOY your customer service is atrocious, and I just ordered another miner from you guys.
Sent from my iphone
Handed to the team · Customer has had two hand-off replies with no answer and is escalating about ser

Ramces,

You are right, and I am not going to argue with you. You asked a clear question, twice, and twice you got a line saying it was passed along with nothing in it. That is on us, not on you, and I am sorry.

So here is the real answer, in writing, today. On the damaged LilyGo, my finding is that a screen broken in transit on a DC02 is a part, not a board fault. The miner itself is fine and stays with you, and only the LilyGo module needs replacing. That finding is recorded on your order and a colleague is picking it up today to confirm the replacement with you directly, since the sending of parts is their call and not mine.

On the flashing problem, you are not locked to hammer miner io. The Hammer DC02 is on the Harlo OS supported model list and DC02 owners flash it regularly, so I found nothing to support the idea that our DC02s ship with eFuses burned and Secure Boot permanently enabled. A flash that errors out on these is almost always the cable, the port or the browser.

What makes it work: flash through the LilyGo's own USB-C port, since the LilyGo is the controller on this miner, with the screen lifted off or the USB connected straight to it. Use a genuine USB data cable, because a charge-only cable powers the board but never shows it to the browser. Open harlolabs.com in Chrome or Edge, pick the DC02 profile, and choose Erase and install with the factory image, not the OTA image, on a first flash. And leave the unit with the broken screen alone for now, because a damaged LilyGo throws errors that look exactly like a firmware fault.

If it still fails after that, send me the exact error text the flasher shows, word for word, plus the browser and the version the page reports, and I will take it from there. JD, our hardware lead, has your case as well. The fastest line to him is our Discord at https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf , mention @nullhashrate.

Hal, HeliumDeploy technical support
